name: Can you refinish custom cabinets instead of replacing them?

mainEntity.name: When is cabinet refinishing a better option than full replacement for high-end kitchens and built-ins?
mainEntity.text: When is cabinet refinishing a better option than full replacement for high-end kitchens and built-ins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Refinishing is a strong option when the cabinet carcasses are still solid and the main issue is color, wear, or style. Many luxury homes choose refinishing for kitchens, vanities, and built-ins when they want a major visual upgrade without the cost and disruption of a full tear-out. It can also be a smart choice when you need to preserve existing stone countertops, flooring, or detailed trim. Full replacement is usually better if the cabinets are swollen from moisture, the drawers and hinges are failing, or the layout no longer fits how the space is used. Before deciding, inspect door condition, veneer integrity, alignment, and any previous paint buildup. Ask whether the shop will spray off-site or on-site, what prep is included, and how the finish will hold up in daily use. The key question is not just cost, but whether the current structure deserves another finish cycle.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cabinet refinishing is often the better option when the box structure is sound, the layout still works, and the existing doors can be sanded, repaired, or resprayed. It is usually less expensive and faster than full replacement. Replacement makes more sense when there is water damage, major warping, poor cabinet layout, or failing box construction.
